description.desc_thousand_char: Pragati Glass & Industries Private Limited (PGIPL), as per its credit rating report, is engaged in the manufacturing of glass bottles, plastic bottles, aluminum tin cans, and UV metalizing. The company has operations in India with its plant for glass bottle manufacturing at Kosamba in Gujarat. It has two furnaces of 80 tons and 90 tons, with a total capacity of 170 tons per day at this plant. The plant in Oman has one furnace with a capacity of 135 tons per day. It also has marketing offices in China and in Dubai. It has a clientele that includes Zandu Pharma, Emami, Godrej, Raymond (J.K. Helen Curtis), Marico, Lykis Ltd, Himalaya Drugs Ltd, and Dabur India Ltd. The company caters to various industries such as cosmetics and perfumes, candles, liquor, and food & beverage. The company was incorporated in 1981 and has its registered office located in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

disclosures_director_report.auditor:
Income Tax authorities conducted survey and search operations in case of the Company during the year.  During these proceedings they have recorded statements of the directors of the company on various dates. In these statements they have admitted unaccounted sales, details of amounts and period to which they relate, are not given to us. These amounts are stated to be used for cash expenses like salaries etc. Several records, including those on electronic media, found with them are inventorised and/or impounded which records are not made available to us. The statements also indicate inflation in cost of materials by overbilling as also cash payments and receipts of unspecified nature, etc.
In view of the above, we understand that there are expenses, income, assets and liabilities which are not recorded or recorded incorrectly in these financial statements. We have also been informed that during later part of the year, such income and expenses have been accounted in books resulting in higher expenses under heads like Remuneration to employees. 
Currently the entire proceedings are under process, and whatever expenses, income, assets and liabilities which are not recorded or recorded incorrectly in the financial statements, consequences of the above under various laws including short provision for taxes and dues under statutory laws including labor laws and their impact on the financial statements cannot be ascertained at this point of time.
As per the Information and explanation provided to us, by the Management, they have opted to go for Settlement Commission and once the petition is filed and accepted, and due decision is taken, company will provide the financial Impact.

The company has made investment of Rs.1,65,00,000/- in equity shares of PG Glass Private Limited, also there is a debit balance of Rs.13,99,19,993/- in their account mainly due to the company having paid the dues of the said company to bank to honor the guarantee given by the company. PG Glass Private Limited has incurred substantial losses and is not currently engaged in the business. No provision is made for losses that the company may incur on account of non-recoverability of whole or part of such amount. Management has not estimated amount realizable on this account hence the loss is not quantified.

We have observed several outstanding in accounts of Customers and Suppliers which appears abnormal in nature due to Non settlement for long periods after considering recoveries after the year end. The values of such outstanding to the extent noticed by us are  as under:

Sr. No	Particulars	                                 Amount (Rs.)
1	Trade Receivable	                                8,31,08,153
2	Trade Payable and other payables	6,03,18,709
3	Advances received from Customers	1,29,41,987
4	Advances given to suppliers	                 50,17,685



We do not have evidence to show whether these balances are confirmed by the parties or any satisfactory explanations regarding the amounts remaining outstanding for long period. Hence, we were unable to form opinion relating to correctness of these values and implications of such outstanding. Further during the year consideration the company has written off amount outstanding in customer and other vendors account amounting to Rs.1,53,14,777 and amount of Rs.2,27,99,865 in suppliers account.

We have relied on quantities and values of inventories as given by the Management as we could not see sufficience evidence of physical verification, reliable  stock records  and input-output control of all items of inventories.
Prescribed disclosures and provisions are not made as regards dues to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

The company has incurred expenditure of Rs.54853903/- for repairs of premises owned by it or by related parties and taken on hire by the Company. The Management has stated that in absence of identifiable fixed assets, no part of such expenditure is capitalized.

disclosures_director_report.auditor:
Income Tax authorities conducted survey and search operations in case of the Company during the year.  During these proceedings they have recorded statements of the directors of the company on various dates. In these statements they have admitted unaccounted sales, details of amounts and period to which they relate, are not given to us. These amounts are stated to be used for cash expenses like salaries etc. Several records, including those on electronic media, found with them are inventorised and/or impounded which records are not made available to us. The statements also indicate inflation in cost of materials by overbilling as also cash payments and receipts of unspecified nature, etc.
In view of the above, we understand that there are expenses, income, assets and liabilities which are not recorded or recorded incorrectly in these financial statements. We have also been informed that during later part of the year, such income and expenses have been accounted in books resulting in higher expenses under heads like Remuneration to employees. 
Currently the entire proceedings are under process, and whatever expenses, income, assets and liabilities which are not recorded or recorded incorrectly in the financial statements, consequences of the above under various laws including short provision for taxes and dues under statutory laws including labor laws and their impact on the financial statements cannot be ascertained at this point of time.
As per the Information and explanation provided to us, by the Management, they have opted to go for Settlement Commission and once the petition is filed and accepted, and due decision is taken, company will provide the financial Impact.

The company has made investment of Rs.1,65,00,000/- in equity shares of PG Glass Private Limited, also there is a debit balance of Rs.13,99,19,993/- in their account mainly due to the company having paid the dues of the said company to bank to honor the guarantee given by the company. PG Glass Private Limited has incurred substantial losses and is not currently engaged in the business. No provision is made for losses that the company may incur on account of non-recoverability of whole or part of such amount. Management has not estimated amount realizable on this account hence the loss is not quantified.

We have observed several outstanding in accounts of Customers and Suppliers which appears abnormal in nature due to Non settlement for long periods after considering recoveries after the year end. The values of such outstanding to the extent noticed by us are  as under:

Sr. No	Particulars	                                 Amount (Rs.)
1	Trade Receivable	                                8,31,08,153
2	Trade Payable and other payables	6,03,18,709
3	Advances received from Customers	1,29,41,987
4	Advances given to suppliers	                 50,17,685



We do not have evidence to show whether these balances are confirmed by the parties or any satisfactory explanations regarding the amounts remaining outstanding for long period. Hence, we were unable to form opinion relating to correctness of these values and implications of such outstanding. Further during the year consideration the company has written off amount outstanding in customer and other vendors account amounting to Rs.1,53,14,777 and amount of Rs.2,27,99,865 in suppliers account.

We have relied on quantities and values of inventories as given by the Management as we could not see sufficience evidence of physical verification, reliable  stock records  and input-output control of all items of inventories.
Prescribed disclosures and provisions are not made as regards dues to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

The company has incurred expenditure of Rs.54853903/- for repairs of premises owned by it or by related parties and taken on hire by the Company. The Management has stated that in absence of identifiable fixed assets, no part of such expenditure is capitalized.
